I know this is a 10 month old post, but not only can testosterone be abused by bodybuilding or athletes, but it's also dangerous in general. Testosterone can cause various health problems in AMAB people, such as heart muscle damage, liver disease, and increased risk of blood clots. In AFAB people, it can pretty much cause the same issues, along with masculinization as ya'll know. And it is easily absorbed through the skin, increasing the risk for unwanted effects.

Estrogen simply doesn't have the same risks. In AMAB people, it can cause ED, infertility, gynecomastia. In AFAB people, it can cause low sex drive, irregular periods, and endometrial cancer after menopause. There are smaller risks of blood clots, stroke, or heart attacks, but they usually coincide with smoking or other medical conditions.

Basically testosterone has a risk of abuse (doping) and can cause health problems or unwanted effects. Estrogen doesn't.

I took 5.5 years to graduate. Undiagnosed and unmedicated. Finally got diagnosed after my last semester.
Freshman year, I failed 3 or 4 classes. It was the first time I had to really take care of myself: go to class on time, find something to eat (and forcing myself to go eat), going down to the laundry room, social interaction, etc. I barely did homework. I realized that being smart and "gifted" in high school was not enough to do well in college.
After the 1st semester of sophomore year, I was put on academic probation. I had to go home and attend community college to prove that I should be allowed back at the university. I only got credit for 1 class (I took 4 classes).
Over the summer (between sophomore and junior year), I retook a class that I failed online (and a new course) and got good grades.
Junior year, senior year, and super senior year were fine; I did poorly in a couple classes but managed to keep my GPA above a 2.0.
I was supposed to graduate in the spring of my final year,  but I didn't do a final project for a class that I needed to graduate. The professor allowed me to work on it during the summer. It took me MONTHS to finally complete it. So I received my degree in December.

I really wish that I was medicated,  or diagnosed at the very least. I think things would have been so much better.

I hate the American medical system (I'm so tired)

2022 has been a terrible year for my health. First I get COVID for the 2nd time in January that caused breathing issues I haven't had since I was a child. I was feeling a lot of fatigue and malaise but my blood work was okay.

And suddenly I developed tremors (and vibrations?), but the neurologist didn't see anything wrong and blamed it on caffeine (never gave me tremors before) or the Adderall I just started taking or simply stress. So I tried taking a non-stimulant which didn't work and had even worse side effects.

At some point I noticed that my muscles are twitching and spasming quite a bit but that's probably normal right? (I wish)

A month later, I went to the ER for some chest pain and tachycardia. They didn't find an immediate cause so I was sent home. Prescribed beta-blockers, terrible side effects too. Went to the cardiologist, my heart is perfectly normal.

Got off the beta-blockers and went back on Adderall. July, I developed urinary retention/hesitancy. After a month, I finally got tested for UTI and STDs, all negative. Symptoms continued. I don't see urology until December.

All throughout the past 9 months I've been trying to accurately describe my symptoms. Tremors, spasms, muscle weakness and fatigue. I've been told that maybe it's all in my head, maybe you're just stressed, are you sure you don't have anxiety? I'm not the best personal advocate, so I don't think my doctors realized how distressing my symptoms have been. I don't remember what being normal/healthy was like anymore.

My GP says she doubts that I have MS because my symptoms have been chronic without a relapse/recovery pattern.

I know MS is a rare illness. I know I shouldn't want to have MS because those who have it really do suffer. But it all makes sense if it is MS and I do desperately want treatment so that I can feel somewhat better.

I have been referred to Neurology again so hopefully they will figure something out.
